origin.description: Rosenbluth concentration coefficient of a numeric vector, also called the Hall–Tideman index.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measure is defined for non-negative values.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: Values are sorted ascending and weighted by n, n-1, ..., 1, so the largest value has weight 1. The coefficient is 1 / (2 * sum(weight * share) - 1). conc() calls this when type is Rosenbluth and ignores parameter.
origin.value: A single number, the Rosenbluth coefficient.
origin.example:
# generate vector (of sales)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
# compute coefficient of Hall/Tiedemann/Rosenbluth
Rosenbluth(x)

translation.description: Rosenbluth concentration coefficient of a numeric vector, also called the Hall–Tideman index.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measure is defined for non-negative values. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result NaN. This is na.rm in R.

translation.details: Values are sorted ascending and weighted by n, n-1, ..., 1, so the largest value has weight 1. The coefficient is 1 / (2 * sum(weight * share) - 1). The sort and the weighted sum use NumPy. conc() calls this when type is Rosenbluth and ignores parameter.
translation.value: A single number, the Rosenbluth coefficient.
translation.example:
from ineq.concentration import Rosenbluth

# generate vector (of sales)
x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
# compute coefficient of Hall/Tiedemann/Rosenbluth
print(Rosenbluth(x))
